Welcome to The Jenny Hammond Primary School.
We know that your child and your family will be happy members of our school community.
The Jenny Hammond Primary School is a small, two-form entry, multicultural community school situated in the southern part of Waltham Forest. Our school comprises children and adults of different faiths and cultures who work happily together. We aim to Engage, Inspire and Empower all of our school community through our curriculum and wider opportunities.
Our school is named after Jenny Hammond who was Mayor of Leyton from 1942-43. She was an active councillor for 35 years and campaigned for just causes throughout her life. The causes that she particularly fought for were those that would benefit the welfare of the local community in Waltham Forest. Jenny Hammond was chair of the Education Committee for 17 consecutive years. She lived close to the school and made regular visits to what were then Cann Hall Infant and Junior schools. She died in her nineties having done much for the communities she served.
Our school is housed in a Victorian building alongside fantastic teaching and learning spaces completed in 2017.
At The Jenny Hammond Primary School we see education as an ongoing process and one that is very much a partnership between school and home. We work tirelessly to build our children’s aspirations and expose them to a range of experiences to help them achieve goals and become successful and we feel proud to have the exciting task of joining with parents and carers in their children’s development.
Providing a child-centred philosophy we treat each child as an individual. Children are organised to work with Learning Partners, small groups, individually or as members of the whole class depending on the learning. We provide a broad and balanced curriculum with high aspirations for all of our children.
We recognise that for our children to feel empowered and be successful academically and in the wider areas of their lives, they need to be given rich and sustained opportunities to develop their cultural capital. We do this in many ways, for example, through our curriculum, extra-curricular activities, trips and visits.
Creativity and mastery in learning sit hand in hand with each other and our children leave Jenny Hammond with the skills needed to succeed in Secondary school and beyond. We are proud of all they achieve and of the young adults they become.
Ofsted had a very positive visit to our school in February 2023 commenting:
'Pupils are happy to attend this school. Teachers think carefully about how to enthuse pupils about their learning. Pupils appreciate this. They talk enthusiastically about their lessons and what they have learned and remembered. Teachers know individual pupils well. They have high expectations for every pupil. The school buzzes with activity.’
The most important people at Jenny Hammond are the children. We look forward to receiving the support of parents and carers and to working with them to inspire all our children to be their best and to realise their full potential.

Music
Vision Statement
At the Jenny Hammond Primary School, we want our children to love music. We want them to have no limits to what their ambitions are and grow up wanting to be music producers, songwriters, composers or rockstars! Our vision, at Jenny Hammond, is to give children access to an engaging and fun music curriculum reflecting the world they live in now, but at the same time giving them access to musical styles throughout history.
The primary aim of Music at Jenny Hammond is that it should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music in all its forms. Children will be exposed to opportunities to listen, appraise, play and perform music throughout their time at JHPS, and it should help them to develop their creativity, imagination and self-confidence. Our intent is to provide children with the opportunity to learn both skills and knowledge within music, so that we might inspire them to become musicians themselves. Our children will be taught music in a way that ensures progression of skills, and follows a sequence to build on previous learning and prepare them as confident musicians for the transition to Secondary.
Some of the many musical opportunities that will be available to your child throughout their time at Jenny Hammond include:
We want our children to leave us with an appreciation of the wonderful benefits and opportunities that music can create!

Design Technology
Vision Statement
At Jenny Hammond Primary School, we believe that Design and Technology prepares children to take part in the development of the rapidly changing world. The subject encourages children to become innovative and creative thinkers and problem-solvers, both as individuals and as part of a team. Our aim is that through the study of Design and Technology our children will combine practical skills with an understanding of aesthetic, social and environmental issues. This allows children to analyse and evaluate past and present designs, its uses and its impacts.

The Jenny Hammond Primary School
ENGAGE INSPIRE EMPOWER
Vision Statement
At The Jenny Hammond Primary School, we believe that English and communication are key life skills. Through our English curriculum, we help children develop the skills and knowledge that will enable them to communicate effectively and creatively through spoken and written language and equip them with the skills to become lifelong learners. We want children to be capable and fluent readers and writers.
We believe that English is central to children’s intellectual, emotional and social development - it has an essential role across the curriculum and helps pupils’ learning to be coherent and progressive. It is at the heart of all children’s learning and enables children both to connect with others effectively for a variety of purposes and to examine their own and others’ experiences, feelings and ideas, giving these order and meaning.

The Jenny Hammond Primary School
ENGAGE INSPIRE EMPOWER
Geography
Vision Statement
All children should leave our school as Geographers who have a sense of their role as the future custodians of planet and the impact they can have on it. Through our curriculum and wider school activities, we will provide purposeful opportunities for exploring, appreciating and understanding the world in which we live. We also intend for children to become passionate and knowledgeable about our local community and have a thorough understanding of places in the wider world, learning through both classroom and practical fieldwork activities. We aim to ensure that through the subject Geography, pupils are able to explore and appreciate the relationship between the Earth and its people, and how they can positively influence their environment.

The Jenny Hammond Primary School
ENGAGE INSPIRE EMPOWER
History
Vision Statement
All children should leave our school as Historians who have a love and a curiosity for History. We aim to stimulate pupils’ interest about the lives of past people and cultures, enabling them to develop their own sense of identity and understanding of their historical heritage. Throughout their time at our school, children learn about aspects of local, British and Ancient history, which allows them to develop a broad awareness and knowledge of historical development in the wider world. All children need an appreciation of their role in multicultural Britain, regardless of their own cultural background, and History plays a vital role in developing the necessary skills and understanding.

pageCache.text:
Elsham Road, Leytonstone, London, E11 3JH
school@jennyhammond.waltham.sch.uk
The Jenny Hammond Primary School
ENGAGE INSPIRE EMPOWER
PE
Subject Lead: Jack Courtney
Jack has been at Jenny Hammond since April 2025, where he also took the role as PE subject lead. In his pervious schools he has led PE and History and has been able to use his experience to develop an exciting and rich PE curriculum at Jenny Hammond. Outside of school he coaches rugby and volunteers as a trustee for 2 local community organisations, where he works to develop coaches who provide both school and community sessions. He understands and values the importance of Physical Education and sport and how this can develop life long skills and confidence.
Jack passionately believes that with right skills and support everyone can access sport and physical activity. His approach to the curriculum is, skills being taught through sports, which allows children to develop confidence in activities whilst exploring a range of sports. He believes that sports and active communities create a sense of belonging for young people. He has worked to ensure pupils have a chance to explore and experience sport and physical activity beyond the school day, with pupils feeling that sport and physical activities are an important part of our school identity.
"PE has helped my confidence grow in other sports" Kyran - Year 5 Pupil
Throughout Jenny Hammond Primary School we strive to develop skills which can be applied in a range of sports and develop opportunities to help create athletes for now and the future. We believe that Physical Education, experienced in a safe, supportive and inclusive environment, is a vital contributor to a child’s physical development and well-being. We believe that a broad and balanced P.E curriculum is essential to provide children with the skills to manage their movement in an active lifestyle and to increase self confidence. At Jenny Hammond Primary School we believe that physical education should be an area of learning where self-esteem, physical progression and positive attitudes to being active and healthy are fostered and nurtured.
At Jenny Hammond Primary School we aim to provide children with a broad and balanced P.E (Physical Education) curriculum; this follows the skills based focus of the National Curriculum and aims to:
"Sport at our school is very important because it helps you to be very healthy and fit. Also our school does a lot of sports events to encourage others." Kattaleya - Year 6 Pupil
How we Teach PE at JHPS
Our programme of learning has been mapped out so that children in EYFS learn fundamental movement, traveling, balancing, catching, sending and striking. In KS1 pupils continue to develop these skills through half termly sports, teaching them that there is a purpose to their learning. In KS2, pupils begin to apply their skills through tactics and decision making and begin to evaluate both their own and other performance. During lessons pupils are taught to reflect on the importance of being active and understanding how different skills can help them to take part in other sports, such as balancing skills developed in gymnastics can help you to play basketball.
Our curriculum is structured so that students can showcase their learning in end of unit events and competitions in school and apply them in fixtures, events and competitions outside of school allowing them to belong and thrive in the subject.
"Exercise helps me to sleep better." Jude - Year 5 Pupil
"PE gets harder each year and we get challenges." Sid - Year 4 Pupil

Elsham Road, Leytonstone, London, E11 3JH
school@jennyhammond.waltham.sch.uk
The Jenny Hammond Primary School
ENGAGE INSPIRE EMPOWER
Science
Vision Statement
At The Jenny Hammond Primary School, we provide high quality teaching through a broad and balanced curriculum. We aim to provide lessons rooted in scientific enquiry with practical hands-on experiences that encourage a deeper understanding and curiosity with questioning. We believe it is vital to promote and develop transferrable skills such as observation, communication and teamwork to evolve the whole child as a lifelong learner. Our objective is to provide lessons which consolidate prior knowledge, encourage deeper understanding and that are rooted in scientific vocabulary. Children will leave our school enthusiastic, passionate science learners who will confidently ask questions and explore the world around them way beyond their time at our school. They will have an understanding that science has changed our lives and that it is vital to the world’s future prosperity. We empower our children so they understand they have the capability to change the world.

Art and Design
Vision Statement
We aim for our children to develop and build their creative confidence throughout their time in our school. We intend to engage, inspire and challenge pupils, equipping them with the understanding and skills to experiment, invent and create their own artistic works. In addition, pupils should develop a deeper understanding of how Art and Design has reflected and shaped our cultural history, and how it contributes to the creative wealth of our world. We want children to enjoy Art and Design in our school, so that they are better equipped for the opportunities, responsibilities and challenges in life beyond primary school.

The Jenny Hammond Primary School

RE
Vision Statement
Our vision is to prepare children to be active and responsible members of society and develop their own self-worth and beliefs while gaining knowledge of, and respect for, different people’s faiths, feelings and values.
The Waltham Forest Syllabus is integrated into the school's curriculum, aiming to provide students with the knowledge and skills needed for life. The Religious Education (RE) curriculum covers various religious beliefs and progressions, promoting social cohesion, respect, and empathy. The teaching is weekly, using the 'big question' method encouraging debates and reasoned argument to helps pupils to understand the place of religion and belief in the modern world.
Teachers use a range of resources to form an enquiry based approach that engages our learners with religious and theological beliefs.
